chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The lowest amount with which a man is cut (amputated) is one-fifth of a Dinar.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for hand amputation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the minimum value (nisab) for the hudud punishment of hand amputation, specifying that the stolen item must be worth at least one-fifth of a Dinar. In Shia jurisprudence, this threshold is critical for distinguishing between minor theft (which may incur discretionary punishment) and major theft warranting the fixed penalty, reflecting the principle of proportionality in divine law. The reliance on the Dinar, a gold coin, underscores the historical economic context while allowing for scholarly interpretation regarding its contemporary equivalent.
